title: Unify backpressure signalling protocol and release-impact mitigation
creator: Sofia Patel
description: Problem: Our Redis consumer groups and Kafka worker pools use different backpressure signals and semantics (visibility timeout vs. lease TTL vs. token-bucket). This leads to cascading latency spikes during bursts, inconsistent retry windows, and complex operational runbooks. We observed two recent incidents where a tenant spike caused cross-tenant queue starvation and downstream SLO breaches. Goal: Design and implement a small, standardized backpressure signalling protocol and a coordinated release-impact mitigation strategy that works across Redis and Kafka ingestion paths without requiring a full rewrite of consumers. Scope: (1) define wire-level signal semantics (soft-shed, hard-shed, drain-start, restore), (2) implement a light-weight coordinator shim that normalizes signals for both Redis and Kafka workers, (3) change retry semantics to use idempotency-token-aware redrive windows and bounded exponential backoff with jitter, (4) provide observability: per-tenant shed-level, token-bucket utilization, and a release-time mitigation mode toggle. Non-goal: Not a full replatforming to a single queue abstraction. Trade-offs: We avoid aggressive per-message durable state (to minimize latency) and accept eventual consistency in shed-state propagation (<= 2s). That keeps implementation smaller but requires stronger testing around race conditions.
acceptance_criteria: Unified signal API documented and published in internal API catalog
Coordinator shim deployed to canary fleet and able to translate Redis/Kafka signals
Per-tenant soft-quota triggers shed at configured thresholds and prevents cross-tenant starvation
Retry windows honor idempotency tokens to prevent duplicate side-effects in 99.9% of cases
Dashboard panels show shed level, token-bucket fill, and moving-latency percentiles by tenant
Feature flag to enable release-impact mitigation and a runbook for toggling
tasks: Design protocol and create confluence design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Backpressure+Signalling+Design
Implement coordinator shim (stateless translator + ephemeral lease store)
Update Redis consumer library to emit/consume unified signals (upgrade redis client as needed)
Update Kafka consumer adapters to respect unified signals and new retry contract
Add unit/integration tests for race conditions and propagated signal delays
Build Grafana dashboards and add synthetic tenant spike tests to CI
Run 2-week canary on non-prod then staged prod with feature flag
notes: Post-incident analysis (2026-02-18): tenant spike in EU caused leak across priority queues due to mismatched visibility/lease semantics. Root cause: consumers exponentially retried without a coordinated shed signal.
Design decision 1 (2026-03-11): Use a small set of signals (soft-shed, hard-shed, drain-start, restore) instead of numeric rates to keep wire protocol simple and interoperable across ecosystems.

Design decision 2 (2026-03-12): Store transient shed state in a leased, in-memory table (ephemeral) with TTL 3s and optional Redis fallback for older clusters to keep latency low and avoid cross-region consistency issues.
Dependency upgrades: bump kafka-clients to 3.9.1, netty to 4.2.90, and redis client to lettuce 7.2. These were chosen for async non-blocking APIs and better flow-control primitives.

Ops checklist for rollout: enable feature flag for 5% traffic -> monitor shed ratio and tail latency -> 25% -> 100%. Abort criteria: >5% increase in 99.9th latency or >1% increase in error-rate for any tenant.
Review notes: PM review (Marco Li) requested clearer tenant isolation metrics and a short roll-back plan. Security review (requested) to confirm no new persistent tokens are introduced.
Open question: whether to expose per-tenant configured thresholds in the Console UI (early preference: start with service-config via API and pilot on Support-managed tenants).
